name: HI-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Tokuda holds a massive fundraising edge: $939K raised and $539K on hand versus Awa's $129K and $7.7K, with no outside spending against her
The district's D+12 lean and a favorable environment for Democrats anchor the fundamentals
Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 95%, the main note of caution in an otherwise one-sided picture
No public general-election polling exists, leaving the forecast reliant on fundamentals
model.rationale: Tokuda's overwhelming money advantage, incumbency, and the district's twelve-point Democratic lean in a friendly environment point to an easy win, and markets price her near-certain despite the absence of polls.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Tokuda or polling showing Awa within single digits would be the first real sign of a contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Jill Tokuda enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by twelve points. She has raised roughly seven times as much as Republican Brenton Awa and holds a large cash-on-hand advantage, with outside groups spending only modestly on her behalf and nothing recorded against her. Prediction markets put her chances around ninety-five percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and incumbency, all of which favor Tokuda. Awa has attracted little outside support, and the national environment leans Democratic this cycle. The main source of uncertainty is the lack of polling data rather than any specific sign of vulnerability, keeping confidence moderate despite the wide expected margin.
